verdicts.note: ARITHMETIC REPRODUCES: from gap_rows30.jsonl, per-minute stranded minutes (rule 4) in run-log aiur+khala = 38.5 h = 14.7% of 261.7 h; Executor present for 68.5%. The CSV top_reason sum is 39.2 h. GAP 9 FACTS ARE PARTLY WRONG. The GitHub timeline confirms agent:rework was labeled at 03:36:25Z by its-applekid, and the next event is the Executor comment and close at 09-18T01:13:13Z. But its-applekid is also the daemon's GitHub identity, and the daemon made the relabel, not the agent. The 2678 agent run ended at 03:05:43Z ('Completed agent task exited normally ... parking replaceable entry'). At 03:06:00Z the daemon logged 'Issue deactivated (human-review): keeping running entry, freeing slot'. At 03:29:19Z the daemon's own ReworkRequeue moved the ticket to human-review. At 03:36:23Z it logged 'CI failure held for reviewed head ... checks=lint'. At 03:36:26Z the lifecycle fence logged 'Stale lifecycle handoff restored while authoritative input is undelivered: observed_state=human-review authoritative_state=rework'; that code path writes the label through Tracker.update_issue_state. The daemon then logged 'dispatch authorization decision=allow' for 2678 on every poll (142 times in the gap), so this was not a label-provenance refusal. It never dispatched 2678 again: the last dispatch was at 02:58:47Z, and telemetry holds only 2 dispatches. The fence was still open at teardown ('admitting for teardown ... authoritative_state=rework', 09-18T01:15Z). The dispatcher itself worked: aiur #2474 was labeled todo at 21:22:45Z and dispatched at 21:24:42Z. Aiur #2678 is therefore a real current-era daemon defect (a parked running entry plus an open fence), about 15.7 h across the 03:36Z, 14:08Z and 16:36Z gaps. Khala #46 on 09-18 has the same human-review-to-rework shape: 2.8 h undispatched until the Executor touched the ticket at 16:00Z. There is no khala daemon text log, so its mechanism is unconfirmed. THE OTHER HALF IS MIS-BUCKETED. Khala 09-16T20:10Z to 09-17T15:15Z (18.9 h, 4 gaps, including gaps 18 and 11) was classified stranded only because 4 tickets (#10 #11 #50 #51) stayed labeled agent:todo. The daemon had dispatched them (telemetry dispatch at 19:23-19:28Z, and #10/#50 again at 21:29Z; workspace_ownership claimed). The fleet showed 4 of 6 slots occupied in every retained sample from 08:25Z to 12:48Z. Their agents had finished local work and sent pause.request 'awaiting repository Write access'. The labels never moved because the agent identity lacked label-write permission (alert at 12:49Z: 'gh issue edit failed: its-applekid lacks AddLabelsToLabelable'). The Executor published and closed all four at 15:35Z. This time is a human permission wait (b/c), not stranded work. The classifier (analyze.py:574-601) takes dispatchability from GitHub labels minus declines and open attention windows. It never checks fleet occupancy or daemon claims, and 'capacity free' means only that no infrastructure window was open. The report itself concedes the problem for #51 in its gap-18 text. GAP 20 (09-10) is in the pre-log era, outside the run-log figure. Its 5 rework tickets include #1767, #2245 and #2413, which were decision-blocked since August. Unverified remainder: about 1.1 h (aiur 09-16 16:57Z, khala 09-24 23:36Z).
verdicts.corrected_claim: In the run-log era for aiur and khala, the report's per-minute classifier puts 38.5 h (14.7 %) of gap time in the stranded bucket, and the Executor was present for 68 % of it. About 18.9 h of that bucket is not stranded work. It is khala on 09-16T20:10Z to 09-17T15:15Z (gaps 18 and 11 and their neighbours). There, the 4 'todo' tickets (#10, #11, #50, #51) had been dispatched and held 4 of 6 fleet slots. Their agents had paused and were waiting for a human decision on repository Write access. The labels stayed agent:todo only because the agent identity could not write labels. That time belongs to waiting on a human. Stranded work with evidence behind it (a rework ticket the daemon did not redispatch while capacity was free) is about 18.5 h, roughly 7 %: aiur #2678 for 15.7 h on 09-17 (03:36Z to 20:55Z) and khala #46 for 2.8 h on 09-18. About 1.1 h more is unverified. The Executor was present for about 60 % of the real part. For #2678, the daemon made the 03:36:25Z relabel to rework, not the agent: its lifecycle fence restored 'rework' while the rework input was still undelivered. The daemon kept a parked running entry for the ticket and allowed dispatch on every poll, but never dispatched it. The ticket stayed stranded until the Executor closed it at 09-18T01:13Z. There was no label-provenance refusal. The dispatcher still worked for other tickets. So this is a current-era daemon defect in the lifecycle-fence and parked-entry path (about 7 % of gap time, on top of the 1.6 % infrastructure share). It is not a general dispatch failure and not an agent-to-daemon label-contract gap. Gap 20 (09-10) is in the pre-log era, and 3 of its 5 rework tickets were blocked on a decision, so it is not an example of the run-log figure.
